content.title: About
content.content: Cacti are succulent plants adapted to arid environments. Cooked cactus without added fat is a tender, slightly crunchy stem portion commonly used in Mexican and Mediterranean dishes. It has a mild, faintly sweet flavor and low calorie density.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The edible parts of most cacti are found in the stem, not the spines.
Cooked cactus (nopales) is a traditional ingredient in Mexican dishes such as “nopalitos”.
Cacti can store water, so their nutritional profile varies with growing conditions.
In some cultures cactus symbolizes resilience and strength.
Spiny parts are often used decoratively but are not edible.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cooked cactus provides very few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber in cactus supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Cactus contains vitamin C, which aids immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Phytochemicals in cactus help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports electrolyte balance
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in cactus contribute to proper fluid balance.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to cactus.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Cactus can contain oxalates, which in excess may promote kidney stone formation.

items.title: Toxicity of certain species
items.content: Not all cactus species are edible; some contain toxic compounds and require proper preparation.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper cooking can allow bacterial growth, so ensure the cactus is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked cactus can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, omelets, or used as a filling for tacos. It is often sliced into rings and lightly sautéed without oil to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cactus in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags to preserve texture and taste.
